title: Shepherd's Pie
subtitle: Minced lamb and rosemary in gravy under a golden mash crust
excerpt: Shepherd's pie is the lamb version of cottage pie: minced lamb with rosemary and vegetables in a rich gravy, topped with buttery mashed potato and baked until golden. Lamb and rosemary is a well-matched combination, and the rendered fat from the mince gives the gravy its depth.
sourceNotes: The shepherd's pie name is recorded in British cookbooks from the mid-nineteenth century, distinguishing the lamb version from the cottage pie made with beef.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze assembled and unbaked for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight, then bake at 180°C fan for 35 minutes until piping hot.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch and freeze one dish for later in the week.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling up to 2 days ahead. Top and refrigerate. Bake straight from the fridge, adding 10 minutes.

content.text: Shepherd's pie is minced lamb braised with onion, carrot, and rosemary in a rich stock, topped with mashed potato and baked golden. It differs from cottage pie in more than just the meat: lamb fat has a different character from beef, and the rosemary gives the filling a clean, herbal note. The name comes from sheep farming rather than any connection to a cottage.

items.prepNote: not too lean (20% fat is ideal)

content.text: Brown {{lamb-mince}} of lamb mince in a large pan over high heat, breaking it up as it colours. The fat will render; pour off the excess if there is a lot. Transfer to a plate.

In the same pan, cook {{onion}} chopped onion and {{carrot}} chopped carrots over medium heat for 8 minutes. Add {{garlic}} of crushed garlic and the chopped rosemary; cook for 1 minute. Stir in {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes.
Return the lamb. Add {{worcestershire-sauce}} of Worcestershire sauce and {{stock-beef}} of stock. Simmer uncovered for 25 minutes until the gravy is thick. Taste and season well.
Boil {{potato}} of potato chunks in salted water until tender, about 18 minutes. Drain and steam dry. Mash with {{unsalted-butter}} of butter and {{whole-milk}} of warm milk. Season well.
Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Spoon the filling into a deep baking dish. Spread the mash on top and fork it into ridges. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and bubbling at the edges.

items.cause: Fatty lamb mince releases a lot of fat during browning.
items.fix: After browning the mince, tilt the pan and spoon off the excess fat before adding the vegetables. Some fat is needed for flavour, but not all.

items.cause: The filling was not simmered long enough to reduce.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered until the gravy coats the back of a spoon with almost no liquid pooling. It will firm up further in the oven.

items.symptom: The mash goes lumpy in the oven
items.cause: The potato was not cooked through before mashing.
items.fix: Make sure the potato is completely tender, not just soft on the outside. Steam it dry in the hot pan for a minute after draining.

items.cause: Too much rosemary, or coarsely chopped rather than finely chopped.
items.fix: Use no more than 2 sprigs' worth of leaves and chop them very finely. Rosemary is powerful and needs restraint.

content.text: Shepherd's pie is a British farming dish, rooted in a time when lamb was the everyday meat of the countryside. It shares a structure with cottage pie but its flavour is its own: the lamb and rosemary combination is older than either of the pie names we use for it today. It is a reliable family supper and one of the best dishes to make on a Sunday afternoon for the week ahead.
